Text 1
The discovery of water ice in permanently shadowed craters near the Moon's south pole has led some planners to envision a lunar base supplied by local resources. The ice could be melted for drinking water or split into hydrogen and oxygen for rocket fuel, greatly reducing the cost of launching supplies from Earth.

Text 2
Planetary scientist Paul Hayne notes that estimates of lunar ice vary widely. Some craters may contain thick deposits, but others may hold ice only as a thin frost mixed into the soil, which would be far more expensive to extract. Until robotic missions measure the deposits directly, he argues, plans that depend on lunar ice rest on uncertain assumptions.
Cross-Text Connections.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Hayne (Text 2) most likely view the plans described in Text 1?
choices: As premature, because the amount and accessibility of the ice have not yet been confirmed
As unrealistic, because water ice cannot be converted into rocket fuel
As well supported, because thick ice deposits have been measured in most craters
As unnecessary, because launching supplies from Earth is becoming less expensive
Cross-Text Connections.expl: Hayne: muz miqdori noaniq, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri o'lchanmagan — rejalar hali erta (premature).

He would argue that women writers of the period never published anonymously.
He would argue that anonymous books sold fewer copies than books published under an author's name.
Cross-Text Connections.expl: Hale erkaklar ham anonim nashr qilganini va tijoriy sabablarni ko'rsatadi — Ruizning izohi to'liq emas bo'lishi mumkin.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1905 novel. Hester has recently moved from the countryside to work in a city shop.
The city did not frighten her, as her mother had predicted it would. What unsettled Hester was something smaller: that no one on the crowded pavements ever looked at anyone else. At home a stranger on the road was an event, to be greeted and discussed for days. Here a thousand strangers passed her every morning, and she began to feel that she, too, was becoming invisible.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Hester is troubled less by the size of the city than by the way its residents ignore one another.
Hester regrets leaving the countryside because she misses her mother.
Hester is frightened by the crowds she encounters on her way to work.
Hester enjoys the anonymity of city life after the constant attention of her village.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Matn aniq aytadi: shahar uni qo'rqitmadi, uni odamlarning bir-biriga qaramasligi bezovta qildi. 'Enjoys' varianti 'unsettled' ga zid.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Geologist Anvar Tursunov studies caves in the Baysun Mountains, where layered mineral deposits called flowstones record changes in rainfall. Because each layer's chemistry reflects the water that formed it, Tursunov can reconstruct wet and dry periods going back 40,000 years. His records show that the region's climate shifted abruptly several times, with some transitions from wet to dry conditions taking less than a century—far faster than earlier models had assumed.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, what did Tursunov's research reveal?
choices: Some major climate shifts in the region occurred more rapidly than had been previously thought.
The chemistry of flowstones varies little from one layer to the next.
The region's climate has been dry for most of the past 40,000 years.
Earlier climate models of the region relied on data from flowstones.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Oxirgi gap: ba'zi o'zgarishlar 100 yildan kam vaqtda bo'lgan — avvalgi modellar taxmin qilganidan tezroq.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: When the city of Bogotá closed more than 100 kilometers of streets to cars every Sunday, officials expected the program to encourage exercise. Surveys found that it did, but they also revealed an effect planners had not anticipated: residents of wealthy and poor neighborhoods, who rarely shared public spaces during the week, mingled on the car-free routes. Researchers now cite the program as an example of how transportation policy can shape social life as well as health.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: A program intended mainly to promote exercise also had a significant social effect.
Closing streets to cars is the most effective way for cities to improve residents' health.
Residents of wealthy neighborhoods in Bogotá exercise more than residents of poor neighborhoods.
Officials in Bogotá designed the car-free program to reduce divisions between neighborhoods.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Dastur jismoniy mashq uchun edi, lekin kutilmagan ijtimoiy natija berdi. Oxirgi variant xato: rasmiylar buni rejalashtirmagan ('had not anticipated').

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1920 essay. The writer is describing an old bookshop.
The proprietor knew the location of every volume, though no catalogue existed and the shelves obeyed no system a customer could discern. Ask him for a book on beekeeping and he would disappear between two leaning stacks, returning minutes later with exactly the volume you wanted—and, more often than not, a second one you had not known you needed.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Based on the text, what is true about the proprietor?
choices: He has a detailed knowledge of his shop's disorganized collection.
He has recently created a catalogue of the books in his shop.
He specializes in selling books about beekeeping.
He is reluctant to help customers who ask for particular books.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Katalog yo'q, tizim ko'rinmaydi, lekin u har bir kitob joyini biladi — tartibsiz to'plamni juda yaxshi biladi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Coral reefs are often described as "rainforests of the sea," and like rainforests they are commonly thought to depend on stable conditions. But marine biologist Tevita Fonua's surveys of reefs around Tonga suggest a more complicated picture. Reefs that had experienced moderate storm damage every few years supported more coral species than either reefs that were rarely disturbed or reefs battered by frequent severe storms. Fonua proposes that occasional disturbance prevents a few fast-growing species from crowding out others.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Research suggests that a moderate level of disturbance may help maintain coral diversity on reefs.
Coral reefs around Tonga are more diverse than rainforests are.
Frequent severe storms are the main threat to coral reefs around Tonga.
Fast-growing coral species are more resistant to storm damage than other species are.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Asosiy g'oya: o'rtacha bezovtalik tur xilma-xilligini saqlaydi. Kuchli bo'ronlar tafsilot, asosiy fikr emas.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1921 essay about the writer's grandfather.
He distrusted any machine he could not take apart. The new tractor stood in the barn for a full season while he studied it, bolt by bolt, filling a notebook with drawings; only when he could have rebuilt it blindfolded did he consent to drive it into the field. My father thought this a waste of a good summer. My grandfather thought it the only honest way to own a thing.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Based on the text, how does the grandfather's view of the tractor differ from the father's?
choices: The grandfather believes that truly owning the tractor requires understanding how it works, whereas the father sees that effort as unnecessary.
The grandfather believes the tractor is poorly made, whereas the father thinks it is reliable.
The grandfather wants to sell the tractor, whereas the father wants to keep it.
The grandfather prefers to farm by hand, whereas the father prefers to use machines.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Bobo mashinani to'liq tushunishni 'yagona halol egalik' deb biladi; ota esa buni yozni isrof qilish deb hisoblaydi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original short story.

Grandfather never threw anything away. The shed behind his house held jars of bent nails, coils of wire, the handles of shovels whose blades had long since rusted through. As a child, Leila had thought it was simply clutter. It was only after the storm, when half the fences on the road were down and the hardware store in town had been closed for a week, that she watched him walk into the shed and return, again and again, with exactly what each neighbor needed.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Leila comes to see that her grandfather's habit of saving things, which she once dismissed, has real value.
Leila's grandfather regrets keeping so many useless items in his shed.
The storm caused the town's hardware store to close permanently.
Leila's neighbors resent her grandfather for refusing to share his tools.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: For decades, the standard account held that the domestication of horses began on the grasslands of Kazakhstan around 5,500 years ago, where the Botai people left behind thousands of horse bones and pottery containing traces of mare's milk. A 2018 genetic study complicated this account. Researchers found that Botai horses were not ancestors of modern domestic horses but of Przewalski's horses, a wild population. Modern domestic horses, it turned out, descend from a different lineage that spread across Eurasia roughly 4,200 years ago.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, what did the 2018 genetic study reveal?
choices: The horses associated with the Botai people are not the ancestors of today's domestic horses.
The Botai people did not keep horses or consume mare's milk.
Przewalski's horses descend from modern domestic horses that escaped into the wild.
Horse domestication began in Kazakhstan more recently than 4,200 years ago.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Tadqiqot: Botai otlari zamonaviy uy otlarining emas, Prjevalskiy otlarining ajdodi. Boshqa variantlar matnga zid.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Urban planners once measured the success of a city street mainly by how quickly cars could move along it. Writer and activist Jane Jacobs challenged this view in the 1960s. She argued that the most successful streets were those with a constant mix of people using them for different purposes at different times of day: shoppers in the morning, office workers at lunch, diners in the evening. Such streets, she wrote, were not only livelier but safer, because they were always watched by many eyes.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Jacobs argued that streets should be judged by how well they support varied human activity rather than by traffic flow.
Jacobs believed that cars should be banned from all city streets.
Urban planners in the 1960s were mainly concerned with public safety.
Jacobs found that office workers were the most important users of city streets.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Jacobs mashinalar tezligi o'rniga ko'chaning turli odamlar tomonidan ishlatilishini muvaffaqiyat mezoni deb bilgan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Octopuses have about 500 million neurons, but roughly two-thirds of them are located not in the brain but in the arms. Studies by neuroscientist Binyamin Hochner and others suggest that each arm can process touch and taste information and coordinate simple movements on its own, even when severed from the body. The brain appears to issue general commands, such as "reach toward that shell," while the arms work out many of the details independently.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Based on the text, which choice best describes how an octopus controls its arms?
choices: The brain gives broad instructions, and the arms handle many specifics of movement themselves.
The brain controls every movement of each arm directly.
The arms act entirely on their own and ignore signals from the brain.
Each arm contains a separate brain that is larger than the central brain.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Miya umumiy buyruq beradi, qo'llar tafsilotlarni o'zi hal qiladi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from an original essay.

We speak of "finding time" as though hours were coins that had rolled beneath the furniture, waiting only to be discovered. But no one has ever found an hour. Time is not found; it is taken from one thing and given to another. The person who says she has no time to read has not been robbed of reading hours by some thief. She has spent them, perhaps wisely, on something else, and the honest question is not where the time went but whether it went where she would have chosen.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Claims about lacking time really reflect choices about priorities, which people should examine honestly.
People who say they have no time to read are usually being dishonest.
Reading is the most valuable way for people to spend their free time.
Most people waste their time on activities they do not enjoy.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Vaqt 'topilmaydi', bir ishdan olinib boshqasiga beriladi — asosiy savol: vaqt biz tanlagan joyga ketdimi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Marine ecologist Ruth Okafor hypothesizes that parrotfish, which scrape algae off coral, help reefs recover after bleaching events by clearing space where new coral larvae can settle. To test the idea, Okafor compared bleached reef sections from which parrotfish had been excluded by cages with nearby bleached sections left open to parrotfish.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
choices: Three years after bleaching, the open sections had significantly more young coral colonies than the caged sections did.
The caged sections contained more species of fish than the open sections did.
Parrotfish were observed feeding more often on healthy coral than on bleached coral.
Algae covered a similar proportion of the caged and open sections three years after bleaching.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza: parrotfish joy ochib, yangi korallar o'sishiga yordam beradi. Ochiq qismda yosh korallar ko'proq bo'lsa — to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tasdiq. Suv o'tlari bir xil bo'lsa, aksincha gipotezani zaiflashtiradi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Some historians have argued that the spread of clocks in eighteenth-century England changed how workers experienced time, making them more conscious of hours and minutes. Historian Priya Nair suggests that this shift happened more gradually than those historians claim, and that many rural workers continued to organize their days by tasks and daylight well into the nineteenth century.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Nair's claim?
choices: Diaries kept by agricultural laborers in the 1820s describe their workdays mainly in terms of completed chores and sunrise and sunset, rarely mentioning clock times.
Clockmakers in eighteenth-century London sold more clocks each decade than they had in the previous decade.
Factory owners in the eighteenth century frequently fined workers for arriving late.
Eighteenth-century clocks were often inaccurate by as much as fifteen minutes a day.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Nair: qishloq ishchilari XIX asrgacha vazifa va kun yorug'ligi bo'yicha yashagan. 1820-yillardagi kundaliklar aynan shuni ko'rsatadi. Zavod jarimalari esa aksincha soatga e'tiborni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Psychologist Mei Lin hypothesized that people remember information better when they explain it aloud to someone else than when they simply reread it, even if the listener asks no questions. In her study, participants studied a passage and then either reread it or explained it to a silent listener; a week later, all participants took the same recall test.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding from Lin's study, if true, would most strongly support her hypothesis?
choices: Participants who explained the passage to a silent listener recalled substantially more of it than did participants who reread it.
Participants who reread the passage spent more total time studying than did participants who explained it.
Participants in both groups rated the passage as equally difficult.
Participants who explained the passage said they enjoyed the task more than did those who reread it.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza eslab qolish haqida — tushuntirgan guruh ko'proq eslab qolgani bevosita tasdiqlaydi. Yoqtirish yoki vaqt esa eslab qolishni o'lchamaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Linguist Rafael Moreno hypothesizes that speakers of languages that mark evidentiality—grammatical markers indicating how a speaker knows a piece of information (for example, by direct observation or by hearsay)—are more attentive to the sources of information in everyday situations than are speakers of languages without such markers. To test this, Moreno showed participants short video clips and later asked them to recall not only what happened but also how they had learned about each event.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Moreno's hypothesis?
choices: Speakers of languages with evidential markers and speakers of languages without them recalled how they had learned about events with similar accuracy.
Speakers of languages with evidential markers recalled the events in the clips more accurately than speakers of other languages did.
Some languages with evidential markers distinguish among more than two sources of information.
Participants in both groups found some video clips more memorable than others.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza: evidentsial tillar egalari manbaga ko'proq e'tibor beradi. Agar ikki guruh manbani bir xil aniqlikda eslasa — gipoteza zaiflashadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Research team A rated each of several published studies of urban heat for how clearly it described its procedures ("transparency") and how closely its temperature categories matched a standard classification ("comparability"). The study by Okafor and Lindgren received high ratings for both transparency and comparability.
The study by Vasquez and colleagues was published more recently than the study by Okafor and Lindgren.
Research team A rated more than a dozen studies of urban heat.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Ikkinchi jamoa xulosasi reytinglarga asoslangan. Agar Okafor va Lindgren ikkala reytingda ham pastroq bo'lsa, xulosa bevosita shubha ostida qoladi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Some researchers have proposed that the long migrations of monarch butterflies are guided by an internal compass that uses the position of the Sun. Because the Sun's position changes throughout the day, such a compass would require the butterflies to have some way of keeping track of time. Biologist Steven Reppert hypothesized that this timekeeping is performed by circadian clocks located in the butterflies' antennae.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Reppert's hypothesis?
choices: Monarchs whose antennae were painted to block light cues flew in random directions, while monarchs with clear-painted antennae flew in the correct direction.
Monarchs that were kept in darkness for several days lost weight more quickly than monarchs kept in normal light.
Monarchs can detect the scent of milkweed plants from a distance of several meters using their antennae.
Monarchs migrate farther in years when temperatures along their route are higher than average.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza: vaqtni mo'ylovlardagi soat kuzatadi. Mo'ylovlarga yorug'lik tushmasa yo'nalish buziladi — to'g'ridan-to'g'ri dalil. Qolganlari vaqt/yo'nalish bilan bog'liq emas.

Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding from Wiessner's study, if true, would most directly support her claim?

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Marine biologists studying sea otters along the California coast have observed that areas with otters tend to have healthier kelp forests. The researchers claim that otters benefit kelp indirectly by eating sea urchins, which graze on kelp and can destroy entire forests when their populations are unchecked.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most strongly support the researchers' claim?
choices: After otters returned to a stretch of coast where they had been absent, urchin numbers there fell sharply and kelp cover increased within a few years.
Sea otters spend a large portion of each day grooming their fur to stay warm in cold water.
Kelp forests grow fastest in water that is cold and rich in nutrients.
Sea urchins are eaten by several species of fish as well as by sea otters.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Some historians have argued that the printing press spread quickly across fifteenth-century Europe mainly because it reduced the cost of producing religious texts for the Church. Economist Jeremiah Dittmar, however, contends that commercial demand was more important, and that presses were established first in major trading cities regardless of their religious significance.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Dittmar's contention?
choices: Cities that were important trade hubs were significantly more likely to have printing presses by 1500 than cities of similar size that were important religious centers but lacked major trade routes.

Printing spread more slowly in regions where fewer people could read.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Dittmar: savdo talabi muhimroq. A savdo shaharlarini diniy markazlar bilan solishtirib, savdo ustunligini ko'rsatadi. B aksincha diniy qarashni qo'llaydi.

A student claims that the most common daily news source differs across age groups, with no single source being the most common for every group.

choices: Social media was the most common source for respondents aged 18–29 (48%), websites for those aged 50–64 (38%), and print for those aged 65 and older (41%).
The share of respondents who read print news daily increased with each older age group.
Among respondents aged 30–49, 34% read news daily on websites.
Fewer than 25% of respondents in every age group read news daily in print, except those aged 65 and older.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo: har xil yosh guruhida eng keng tarqalgan manba har xil. Birinchi variant uch guruhdagi uch xil 'eng ko'p' manbani ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Political scientists hypothesized that local governments are far more likely to offer incentives to a company when the company's expansion would be announced shortly before an election, when officials could take credit for it. The researchers sent inquiries to about 1,300 municipalities in each of two conditions: the company said it would announce its expansion either just before or just after the next local election.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that weaken the researchers' hypothesis?
choices: The numbers of municipalities that offered incentives were nearly the same whether the announcement was planned for before or after the election.
Most municipalities in both conditions did not respond to the inquiry at all.
More municipalities replied without an offer when the announcement was planned for before the election than when it was planned for after.
Fewer than 100 municipalities offered incentives when the announcement was planned for after the election.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Gipotezaga ko'ra 'saylovdan oldin' shartida takliflar ancha ko'p bo'lishi kerak edi. Ikkala shartda deyarli bir xil (90 va 85) — bu gipotezani zaiflashtiradi. B variant to'g'ri ma'lumot, lekin gipotezaga aloqasi yo'q.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Botanist Leila Ahmadi suspected that heat, rather than visits from pollinators, is the main reason nectar in a desert wildflower declines over the course of a day. She covered some plants with shade cloth and left others exposed to the sun, preventing pollinators from reaching all of the flowers, and measured nectar volume at three times of day. Ahmadi concluded that her data supported her suspicion.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support Ahmadi's conclusion?
choices: Even though pollinators could not reach any of the flowers, nectar volume in sun-exposed plants fell from 2.3 to 0.9 microliters over the day, while it stayed near 2.5 microliters in shaded plants.
In the morning, shaded plants and sun-exposed plants had similar nectar volumes.
Shaded plants had slightly more nectar at midday than they did in the morning.
Sun-exposed plants had less nectar in the evening than shaded plants did in the morning.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Changlatuvchilar hech bir gulga yeta olmagan, demak kamayish issiqlikdan. Faqat quyoshdagi o'simliklarda kamayish va soyadagilarda barqarorlik — xulosani to'liq qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Urban planner Sofia Marchetti studied bike-share programs in two cities. She noticed that ridership in City B, which had built protected bike lanes before 2018, grew steadily every year, whereas ridership in City A, which added protected lanes only in 2021, was more volatile. Marchetti suggests that protected lanes help a program keep riders even when outside conditions change.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support Marchetti's suggestion?
choices: In 2020, trips per day fell from 14,000 to 9,000 in City A but rose from 9,000 to 11,000 in City B.
City A had more trips per day than City B in every year except 2020.
Trips per day in City A were higher in 2022 than in any other year shown.
Both cities had more trips per day in 2022 than in 2018.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Taklif: himoyalangan yo'laklar tashqi sharoit o'zgarganda ham chavandozlarni saqlaydi. 2020 yilda A shahrida keskin tushish, B da o'sish — aynan shuni ko'rsatadi. Boshqa variantlar to'g'ri ma'lumot, lekin taklifga aloqasi yo'q.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Agronomist Kwame Asante compared farm plots planted with cover crops (plants grown between main crops to protect soil) with plots left bare. At the start of the growing season, both types of plots had similar soil moisture. Asante concluded that cover crops help soil retain moisture as the season becomes hotter and drier: ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
choices: by August, soil moisture had fallen to 23% in plots with cover crops but to 15% in plots without them.
in April, soil moisture was 31% in plots with cover crops and 32% in plots without them.
soil moisture in plots with cover crops decreased each month from April to August.
plots without cover crops had lower soil moisture in June than in May.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Xulosa: issiq va quruq davrda qoplama ekinlar namlikni saqlaydi. Avgustdagi farq (23% va 15%) buni ko'rsatadi. B variant boshlang'ich holat — xulosani qo'llab-quvvatlamaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Researchers tested whether planting strips of wildflowers next to crop fields increases the number of native bees visiting the crops. They counted bee visits to blueberry flowers in fields with and without wildflower strips over three years. They concluded that the benefit of the strips grew over time as bee populations became established.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers' conclusion?
choices: The difference in bee visits between fields with strips and fields without strips increased from Year 1 to Year 3.
Fields without wildflower strips received some bee visits in every year of the study.
In Year 1, fields with strips received more bee visits than fields without strips.
The number of bee visits to fields without strips was about the same in Year 1 and Year 3.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Xulosa: foyda vaqt o'tib ortgan. Farq: 1-yil 4, 2-yil 13, 3-yil 25 — farqning o'sishi aynan shuni ko'rsatadi. C faqat 1-yilni aytadi.

They compared adults aged 60 to 64, who were not eligible for free passes, with adults aged 65 to 69, who were eligible. The team claims that free passes mainly led people to make new trips rather than replacing trips they previously made by car.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Ecologists measured the survival of oak seedlings planted in a forest under three conditions: in open areas, under shrubs, and in areas surrounded by fences that kept out deer. A student claims that, in this forest, protection from deer mattered more for seedling survival than shade did.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the student's claim?
choices: Survival after three years was far higher for fenced seedlings than for seedlings under shrubs, which survived only slightly better than seedlings in open areas.
Survival declined each year for seedlings in all three conditions.
Seedlings in open areas had the lowest survival rate after one year.
More than half of the seedlings under shrubs survived the first year.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo: bug'udan himoya soyadan muhimroq. 3-yilda: to'siqli 71%, buta ostida 24%, ochiq 18% — to'siq katta farq beradi, soya esa kichik.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: A city library began offering evening hours in 2021. A report claims that the change attracted new visitors rather than simply shifting existing visitors to later times.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the report's claim?
choices: Daytime visits stayed about the same after 2021, while total visits rose because of the added evening visits.
Evening visits were lower in 2021 than in 2023.
Daytime visits were higher than evening visits in every year shown.
Total visits in 2020 were lower than total visits in 2019.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Agar tashrif buyuruvchilar shunchaki kechga ko'chganda edi, kunduzgi tashriflar kamayardi. Kunduzgi ~ 40 da qolgan, jami esa oshgan — yangi tashrif buyuruvchilar.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Scientists compared the average body length of a species of lizard on islands with different numbers of predator species. They hypothesized that lizards evolve longer legs relative to body length on islands with more predators, since longer legs allow faster running.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the scientists' hypothesis?
choices: Relative leg length increased as the number of predator species increased, while body length stayed about the same.
Lizards on Island D had the greatest average body length.
Island A had the fewest predator species of the four islands.
Body length varied by less than 2 millimeters across the islands.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Gipoteza oyoq nisbiy uzunligi yirtqichlar soni bilan ortadi. Jadvalda 0.41 → 0.47 → 0.52 → 0.58, tana uzunligi deyarli bir xil.

Inferences.passage: Archaeologists excavating a Bronze Age settlement found hundreds of loom weights, the clay objects used to hold threads taut during weaving. Yet the settlement's soil contained almost no traces of the flax or wool fibers that weavers would have used, and no remains of sheep were found among the animal bones at the site. Because loom weights are heavy and were rarely transported far, the archaeologists concluded that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the settlement's weavers likely obtained their fibers from somewhere other than the settlement itself.
the loom weights were probably used for a purpose other than weaving.
the settlement's residents probably did not wear woven clothing.
sheep must have been raised at the settlement but their bones were not preserved.
Inferences.expl: To'quvchilik joyida bo'lgan (og'ir toshlar uzoqqa tashilmagan), lekin tola va qo'y yo'q — demak tolani boshqa joydan olishgan. 'Bones not preserved' matn dalillariga zid taxmin.

Inferences.passage: In many bird species, females prefer males with elaborate songs. Researchers studying a species of warbler found that males raised in noisy urban areas sang simpler songs than rural males did, but urban females did not show a weaker preference for complex songs when tested in quiet conditions. If complex songs continue to signal male quality to females, ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: urban males may be at a disadvantage in attracting mates compared with rural males.
urban females will likely begin to prefer simpler songs within a few generations.
rural males will likely begin singing simpler songs to compete with urban males.
noise has no effect on which males are chosen as mates.
Inferences.expl: Shahar erkaklari soddaroq kuylaydi, urg'ochilar esa baribir murakkab kuyni afzal ko'radi — demak shahar erkaklari juft topishda noqulay holatda bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: A company tested two versions of its website. Version A displayed prices including tax, while version B displayed prices before tax and added tax at checkout. Visitors to version B added more items to their carts, but a larger share of them abandoned their carts at checkout. The company's analysts noted that total sales were nearly identical for the two versions, suggesting that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the additional items placed in carts on version B were largely offset by the higher rate at which those carts were abandoned.
visitors to version A added more items to their carts than visitors to version B did.
displaying prices before tax has no effect on how shoppers behave.
most shoppers do not notice whether displayed prices include tax.
Inferences.expl: B da savat ko'proq to'ldi, lekin ko'proq tashlab ketildi, umumiy savdo esa bir xil — demak biri ikkinchisini qoplagan. 'No effect' xato, chunki xatti-harakat o'zgargan.

Inferences.passage: Glaciologists drilling into an Antarctic ice sheet found a layer of volcanic ash about 1,000 meters below the surface. The ash's chemistry matches that of a known eruption in New Zealand, which other evidence dates to roughly 25,000 years ago. Because ice layers accumulate from the surface downward over time, the ice directly above the ash layer ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: must have formed less than roughly 25,000 years ago.
must have formed more than roughly 25,000 years ago.
was likely formed from ash deposited by the same eruption.
is probably thicker than the ice directly below the ash layer.
Inferences.expl: Muz yuqoridan pastga to'planadi, demak kul ustidagi muz kuldan keyin, ya'ni 25 000 yildan kamroq vaqt oldin hosil bo'lgan.

Inferences.passage: In many desert plants, a type of photosynthesis called CAM allows leaves to open their pores only at night, when cooler air reduces water loss. Botanist Salma Haddad found that one shrub species switches to CAM only during droughts, using ordinary daytime photosynthesis when water is plentiful. Because ordinary photosynthesis supports faster growth but loses more water, Haddad's finding suggests that the shrub ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: trades rapid growth for water conservation only when conditions make conservation necessary.
grows more quickly during droughts than when water is plentiful.
is unable to survive in regions where droughts are common.
loses less water during wet periods than other desert plants do.
Inferences.expl: Suv ko'p bo'lsa tez o'sish (oddiy fotosintez), qurg'oqchilikda suvni tejash (CAM) — ya'ni o'simlik faqat zarur bo'lganda tezlikni tejashga almashtiradi.

Inferences.passage: Historians studying medieval trade have relied heavily on surviving merchant contracts, most of which were drawn up by notaries in large port cities such as Genoa and Venice. Economic historian Nadia Sorensen notes, however, that small inland traders rarely used notaries, often sealing agreements orally or with brief informal notes that were seldom preserved. If Sorensen is correct, reconstructions of medieval commerce based mainly on notarial contracts ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: may overrepresent the activity of large coastal merchants relative to that of small inland traders.
are likely to underestimate the importance of port cities such as Genoa and Venice.
should be replaced by studies of inland traders' oral agreements, which were carefully preserved.
demonstrate that small inland traders were more numerous than coastal merchants.
Inferences.expl: Saqlangan shartnomalar asosan port shaharlaridagi notariuslardan — kichik ichki savdogarlar deyarli qayd etilmagan. Demak manbalar yirik qirg'oq savdogarlarini ortiqcha aks ettiradi.

Inferences.passage: Most of the ancient Roman concrete that survives today contains small white lumps of lime. Scholars long assumed these lumps were signs of careless mixing. But a team led by Admir Masic found that when cracks form in the concrete and water seeps in, the lime lumps dissolve and recrystallize as calcium carbonate, filling the cracks. This finding suggests that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: features once regarded as flaws in Roman concrete may have contributed to its durability.
Roman builders deliberately added water to their concrete to make it stronger.
modern concrete contains more lime than Roman concrete did.
most Roman concrete structures were built without any lime.
Inferences.expl: Nuqson deb hisoblangan ohak bo'laklari yoriqlarni to'ldiradi — demak ular mustahkamlikka hissa qo'shgan bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: In a series of experiments, psychologist Ellen Langer gave residents of a nursing home a houseplant. Residents in one group were told that they were responsible for watering and caring for the plant and could make choices about their daily schedules; residents in a second group were told that the staff would care for the plant and make those decisions for them. Eighteen months later, residents in the first group were more active and alert than those in the second group. If the groups were otherwise similar, the results suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: having a sense of control over one's environment may benefit the well-being of older adults.
caring for houseplants is more beneficial than any other activity for nursing home residents.
nursing home staff are generally unable to care for plants properly.
residents in the second group disliked the plants they were given.
Inferences.expl: Guruhlar orasidagi farq — nazorat va tanlov imkoniyati. Demak nazorat hissi foydali bo'lishi mumkin. B haddan tashqari keskin.

Inferences.passage: Glaciers in the Himalayas supply meltwater to rivers that serve hundreds of millions of people. As the climate warms, the glaciers are melting faster, which in the short term increases the flow of water in these rivers. However, the glaciers are also shrinking, and once they lose enough mass, less ice will be available to melt each summer. Thus, communities that currently benefit from increased river flow should expect that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the flow of water from glacial melt will eventually decline.
rivers in the region will continue to rise indefinitely.
the Himalayan glaciers will begin growing again once rivers reach their peak flow.
the amount of rainfall in the region will decrease.
Inferences.expl: Hozir erish ko'paydi, lekin muzliklar kichraysa, eriydigan muz kamayadi — oqim oxir-oqibat kamayadi.

Inferences.passage: The Voynich manuscript, a fifteenth-century book written in an unknown script, has resisted decades of attempts at decipherment. Some researchers have suggested it is an elaborate hoax containing meaningless text. However, statistical analyses show that the frequency of its words follows the same pattern found in natural languages, in which a few words appear very often and most words appear rarely. Because a forger working in the fifteenth century would have been unlikely to know about such patterns, these analyses suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the manuscript is more likely to contain meaningful language than random text.
the manuscript was written in a language that is still spoken today.
the manuscript was produced much later than the fifteenth century.
statistical analysis will soon allow researchers to fully translate the manuscript.
Inferences.expl: Tabiiy tillarga xos statistik naqsh bor, soxtakor buni bilmagan bo'lardi — demak matn ma'noli bo'lishi ehtimoli yuqori. D haddan oshiq.

Inferences.passage: Tardigrades, microscopic animals that can survive extreme dehydration, produce a protein called Dsup that binds to their DNA. When researchers inserted the gene for Dsup into human cells grown in a laboratory, the cells suffered about 40% less DNA damage from X-rays than unaltered cells did. This result suggests that, in tardigrades, Dsup likely ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: helps protect the animals' DNA from damage.
allows the animals to survive without water permanently.
is produced only when the animals are exposed to X-rays.
causes the animals' cells to divide more rapidly.
Inferences.expl: Dsup inson hujayralarida DNK zararlanishini kamaytirdi — tardigradlarda ham DNK ni himoya qilishi ehtimoli bor.

Boundaries.passage: The Aral Sea, once the fourth-largest lake in the world, began shrinking in the 1960s when the rivers that fed it were diverted for ______ by 2007, it had lost roughly 90 percent of its volume.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: irrigation;
irrigation,
irrigation
irrigation, and,
Boundaries.expl: Ikki mustaqil gap ('The Aral Sea ... began shrinking' va 'it had lost...') bog'lovchisiz birlashtirilganda nuqtali vergul kerak. Vergul bilan — comma splice.

Boundaries.passage: Among the materials the sculptor collected for her installation were driftwood from the Maine coast, rusted hinges salvaged from a demolished ______ and several hundred glass bottles, each tinted a slightly different shade of green.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: barn,
barn;
barn
barn:
Boundaries.expl: Bu uch elementli ro'yxat (driftwood, hinges, bottles), elementlar oddiy vergul bilan ajratiladi. Nuqtali vergul faqat elementlar ichida vergul bo'lsa ishlatiladi.

Boundaries.passage: The mathematician's proof, which ran to more than two hundred pages and relied on computer calculations that no human could check by ______ was accepted only after independent teams had verified it using different software.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: hand,
hand
hand;
hand—
Boundaries.expl: 'which ran ... by hand' — bu qo'shimcha izoh qismi; u vergul bilan boshlangan, shuning uchun vergul bilan yopilishi kerak.

Boundaries.passage: Botanist Lena Petrova's experiments revealed something unexpected about the desert ______ its seeds can remain dormant in the soil for more than a decade, germinating only after a rainfall of at least 25 millimeters.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: marigold:
marigold, and
marigold
marigold, that
Boundaries.expl: Birinchi qism 'something unexpected' deb e'lon qiladi, ikkinchi qism uni tushuntiradi — bu holatda ikki nuqta ishlatiladi.

Boundaries.passage: In 1976, the Viking 1 lander became the first spacecraft to operate successfully on the surface of ______ transmitting images and weather data to Earth for more than six years, it far outlasted its planned ninety-day mission.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: Mars;
Mars,
Mars
Mars, and
Boundaries.expl: 'transmitting ... six years' ikkinchi mustaqil gapning boshi (it far outlasted...). Ikki mustaqil gap orasida nuqtali vergul kerak.

Boundaries.passage: The novelist's archive, which scholars had assumed was lost in a 1943 ______ turned up in 2019 in the basement of a Lisbon bookshop, its letters and manuscripts remarkably intact.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: fire,
fire
fire;
fire—
Boundaries.expl: 'which scholars had assumed was lost in a 1943 fire' — vergul bilan boshlangan izoh qismi; u vergul bilan yopilishi kerak.

Boundaries.passage: In 1911, explorer Hiram Bingham reached Machu Picchu, a fifteenth-century Inca citadel high in the Andes of Peru. Although Bingham is often credited with discovering the site, local farmers had long known about ______ a family was living and farming on its terraces when he arrived.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: it;
it,
it
it, and,
Boundaries.expl: Ikki mustaqil gap: '...long known about it' va 'a family was living...'. Ularni nuqta-vergul bog'laydi. Vergul yolg'iz — comma splice.

Boundaries.passage: The painter's final series consists of twelve canvases, each depicting the same stretch of ______ at a different hour of the day, from the gray stillness of dawn to the deep violet of late evening.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: coastline
coastline,
coastline;
coastline:
Boundaries.expl: 'the same stretch of coastline at a different hour' — bir butun ibora, orasiga tinish belgisi kerak emas.

Boundaries.passage: Marine biologist Ayana Elizabeth Johnson has argued that addressing climate change requires more than technical ______ it also requires building coalitions among people with different skills, from engineers and farmers to artists and teachers.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: solutions;
solutions,
solutions
solutions, and
Boundaries.expl: '...more than technical solutions' va 'it also requires...' — ikki mustaqil gap. Ularni nuqta-vergul ajratadi; faqat vergul qo'yish — comma splice.

Boundaries.passage: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is not a solid island of trash, as it is sometimes ______ instead, it is a vast area in which small plastic fragments are suspended throughout the upper layers of the water.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: imagined;
imagined,
imagined
imagined, and
Boundaries.expl: 'Instead' bilan boshlangan yangi mustaqil gap: oldidan nuqta-vergul (yoki nuqta) kerak.

Boundaries.passage: Among the objects recovered from the shipwreck were a bronze astrolabe, used for navigation; several ceramic ______ and a small wooden chest that still contained coins from three different countries.
Boundaries.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: jars, many of them intact;
jars, many of them intact,
jars; many of them intact,
jars many of them intact;
Boundaries.expl: Ro'yxat elementlari ichida vergul bor, shuning uchun elementlar nuqta-vergul bilan ajratiladi: '...navigation; several ceramic jars, many of them intact; and...'.

Form, Structure, and Sense.passage: The collection of letters, diaries, and photographs that the historian discovered in a family attic ______ a rare glimpse into daily life in a nineteenth-century mining town.
Form, Structure, and Sense.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: offers
offer
are offering
have offered
Form, Structure, and Sense.expl: Ega — 'The collection' (birlik). 'letters, diaries, and photographs' faqat uning tarkibi, shuning uchun fe'l birlikda: 'offers'.

Form, Structure, and Sense.passage: Neither the museum's director nor its board members ______ willing to comment on reports that the painting had been misattributed for more than a century.
Form, Structure, and Sense.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: were
was
is
has been
Form, Structure, and Sense.expl: 'Neither ... nor' da fe'l yaqinroq egaga moslashadi: 'board members' (ko'plik) → 'were'. O'tgan zamon matndagi 'had been' bilan mos.

Form, Structure, and Sense.passage: Having spent a decade photographing glaciers in Patagonia, ______ the dramatic retreat of the ice to a wide audience.
Form, Structure, and Sense.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: Eleni Vasquez published a book that documented
a book was published by Eleni Vasquez that documented
the book that Eleni Vasquez published documented
Eleni Vasquez's book documented
Form, Structure, and Sense.expl: 'Having spent a decade photographing' ni bajargan shaxs darhol vergul ortidan kelishi kerak — Eleni Vasquez. Kitob o'n yil suratga olmagan (dangling modifier).

Form, Structure, and Sense.passage: When the ancient city of Merv was at its height in the twelfth century, travelers who arrived at ______ gates described markets filled with silk, spices, and manuscripts from across Asia.
Form, Structure, and Sense.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: its
it's
their
they're
Form, Structure, and Sense.expl: Olmosh 'the ancient city of Merv' (birlik) ga qaytadi va egalikni bildiradi: 'its'. 'It's' = 'it is'.

Form, Structure, and Sense.passage: Each of the twelve tapestries in the museum's newly restored series ______ a different month of the year, from January's snow-covered fields to December's candlelit feasts.
Form, Structure, and Sense.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: depicts
depict
are depicting
have depicted
Form, Structure, and Sense.expl: Ega — 'Each' (birlik), 'tapestries' emas. Shuning uchun birlikdagi fe'l: 'depicts'.

Form, Structure, and Sense.passage: By the time the archaeologists finished excavating the site in 2015, they ______ more than 4,000 artifacts, including pottery, tools, and fragments of woven cloth.
Form, Structure, and Sense.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: had recovered
recover
will have recovered
are recovering

Transitions.passage: The composer insisted that her symphony be performed without an intermission, arguing that a break would destroy its carefully built tension. Many orchestras, worried that audiences would grow restless during the ninety-minute work, ignored her instructions. ______ the few performances that honored her wishes were, by most accounts, the most powerful.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Tellingly,
Similarly,
For instance,
As a result,
Transitions.expl: Uning talabini bajargan ijrolar eng kuchli bo'lgani — bastakorning fikrini tasdiqlaydigan muhim dalil. 'As a result' xato, chunki orkestrlarning e'tiborsizligi bunga sabab emas.

Transitions.passage: For much of the twentieth century, scientists believed that adult human brains could not grow new neurons. Studies in the 1990s found evidence of new neurons forming in the hippocampus, a region involved in memory. ______ some researchers now question those findings, arguing that the techniques used to identify young neurons may have produced false positives.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Even so,
Consequently,
In other words,
Likewise,
Transitions.expl: Yangi topilmalar bor, ammo ba'zi olimlar ularni shubha ostiga oladi — bu qarama-qarshilik, 'Even so'. 'Consequently' sabab-natijani bildiradi, bu yerda yo'q.

Transitions.passage: The Silk Road is often imagined as a single highway linking China and the Mediterranean. In reality, it was a shifting web of routes, and few merchants traveled its full length. ______ goods typically passed through many hands, changing owners at oasis towns such as Samarkand and Bukhara before reaching distant markets.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Instead,
Nevertheless,
Moreover,
Meanwhile,
Transitions.expl: Savdogarlar to'liq yo'lni bosib o'tmagan; uning o'rniga mollar ko'p qo'llardan o'tgan — 'Instead'. 'Moreover' shunchaki qo'shimcha fikr, bu yerda almashtirish ma'nosi kerak.

Transitions.passage: Early critics dismissed the photographer's blurred, grainy street scenes as technically incompetent. The photographer, for her part, had deliberately used slow shutter speeds and cheap film to capture the motion and confusion of city life. ______ what critics saw as mistakes were, in fact, her central artistic choices.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: In other words,
Nonetheless,
Additionally,
By contrast,
Transitions.expl: Oxirgi gap oldingi fikrni boshqacha so'z bilan xulosalaydi (xato deb ko'rilgan narsa — ataylab tanlov) — 'In other words'.

Transitions.passage: Early studies of the drug suggested that it reduced symptoms in nearly 70 percent of patients. These studies, however, did not include a control group receiving a placebo. When later trials added such a group, the drug's apparent effect shrank considerably. ______ much of the improvement seen in the early studies may have reflected patients' expectations rather than the drug itself.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: In other words,
Nevertheless,
By contrast,
Similarly,
Transitions.expl: Oxirgi gap oldingi dalillardan chiqqan xulosani boshqacha ifodalaydi — 'In other words'. 'Nevertheless' qarama-qarshilik bildiradi, bu yerda yo'q.

Transitions.passage: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is often imagined as a floating island of trash. In fact, most of its plastic consists of tiny fragments suspended below the surface, invisible from a passing ship. ______ satellite images, which can reveal large debris fields, are of limited use for measuring the patch's extent.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: For this reason,
Moreover,
Instead,
Still,
Transitions.expl: Plastik suv ostidagi mayda bo'laklar bo'lgani uchun sun'iy yo'ldosh suratlari foydasi kam — sabab-natija: 'For this reason'.

Transitions.passage: For much of the twentieth century, doctors advised patients with back pain to rest in bed until the pain subsided. Studies conducted since the 1990s, ______ have found that patients who remain moderately active tend to recover more quickly than those who rest.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: however,
for example,
similarly,
in other words,
Transitions.expl: Avvalgi maslahat (dam olish) va yangi topilma (faol bo'lish yaxshi) qarama-qarshi: 'however'.

Transitions.passage: The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth; some weather stations there have never recorded rainfall. ______ astronomers have built several of the world's most powerful telescopes in the region, since the dry, cloudless skies provide exceptionally clear views of space.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Consequently,
Nevertheless,
Meanwhile,
Likewise,
Transitions.expl: Quruq, bulutsiz osmon — shuning uchun teleskoplar qurilgan: natija, 'Consequently'. 'Nevertheless' mantiqqa zid, chunki quruqlik to'siq emas, sabab.

Transitions.passage: Honeybees communicate the location of food through a movement called the waggle dance. The angle of the dance indicates the direction of the food relative to the Sun. ______ the duration of the dance's waggling portion indicates the distance to the food.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Additionally,
Instead,
As a result,
Nonetheless,

Transitions.passage: Some critics predicted that e-books would make printed books obsolete. Sales of e-books grew rapidly between 2008 and 2013. ______ they then leveled off, and printed books continue to account for the majority of book sales in many countries.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: After that, though,
For instance,

In fact,
Transitions.expl: O'sishdan keyin to'xtash — vaqt ketma-ketligi va kutilganga zid: 'After that, though'.

Transitions.passage: The city's new bike lanes were intended to reduce car traffic downtown. Two years after their installation, traffic counts on major streets had dropped by 12 percent. ______ the number of cyclists commuting downtown had nearly doubled.
Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Over the same period,
In contrast,
Even so,
Previously,
Transitions.expl: Ikki natija bir vaqtda sodir bo'lgan va bir-birini to'ldiradi: 'Over the same period'. 'In contrast' noto'g'ri, chunki ikkisi zid emas.

Rhetorical Synthesis.passage:

  • The Great Green Wall is an initiative to restore land across Africa's Sahel region.

  • Its original goal was to plant a continuous belt of trees 8,000 kilometers long.
  • Planners later shifted to a mosaic of land-restoration projects, such as water-harvesting and farmer-managed tree regrowth.
  • The shift was made because many planted seedlings died in dry conditions.
Rhetorical Synthesis.prompt: The student wants to explain why the initiative's approach changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Because many seedlings planted for the Great Green Wall died in dry conditions, planners moved away from a continuous belt of trees toward a mosaic of land-restoration projects.
The Great Green Wall, launched by the African Union in 2007, originally aimed to plant a belt of trees 8,000 kilometers long across the Sahel.
The Great Green Wall now includes projects such as water-harvesting and farmer-managed tree regrowth.
Launched in 2007, the Great Green Wall is an African Union initiative to restore land across the Sahel region.
Rhetorical Synthesis.expl: Maqsad — nima uchun yondashuv o'zgarganini tushuntirish: sabab (ko'chatlar nobud bo'ldi) va o'zgarish (belbog'dan mozaikaga) birga bo'lishi kerak.
